Upcoming Federal Changes to MaineCare Eligibility for Some Non-citizens

Aug 20, 2026

We are writing to inform you about an upcoming change to MaineCare eligibility that may affect some of your MaineCare patients. This change is required by federal legislation signed into law in July 2025 (also called H.R.1, One Big Beautiful Bill, P.L.119-21, or Working Families Tax Cuts Act) that made changes to the Medicaid program nationally. These changes apply in all states, including Maine.

Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

Maine Financial Institutions Superintendent warns consumers of financial scams related to the anticipated direct payments from the U.S. Government under the CARES Act

May 6, 2020

GARDINER – Superintendent of the Maine Bureau of Financial Institutions Lloyd LaFountain is warning consumers of an expected surge in scam attempts involving the anticipated direct payment to individuals under the federal Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act or the CARES Act. The new law, enacted by Congress on March 27, 2020, is intended to provide financial relief to all Americans to help alleviate the negative economic impact of the coronavirus pandemic. Individuals can expect to receive a direct payment from the federal government in amounts up to $1,200 beginning in the next few weeks.

“Unfortunately, scammers will very likely try to exploit the program to engage in ID theft and to defraud innocent people of their payments. Everyone is reminded to remain vigilant during the current crisis and be wary of any requests for personal information,” remarked LaFountain.

The Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service have announced that distribution of economic impact payments will begin in the next three weeks and will be distributed automatically, with no action required for most people. The IRS indicates that Social Security beneficiaries who are not typically required to file tax returns will not need to file to receive a payment. Instead, payments will be automatically deposited into their bank accounts. However, some people who typically do not file returns will need to submit a simple tax return to receive the economic impact payment. Details on how to obtain the payments will be posted on the IRS website. The Superintendent urges Mainers to go to www.IRS.gov for their information.

Consumers should be on the lookout for mailings, emails, phone calls, and other communications from fraudsters claiming to provide consumers quick access to economic impact payments. You should never provide personal account information or other personal information in response to an unsolicited e-mail, text, or call. Government agencies, financial institutions, and other legitimate organizations do not request personal account information in such a manner.

To protect your money and prevent identity theft remember:

  • Do not click on links in an email or text message unless you are confident it is not a scam. Clicking the link itself may expose your personal information to scammers and harmful software.
  • Never provide personal account information or other personal information in response to an e-mail, text, or call. A bank or credit union does not request personal account information in such a manner.
  • Ignore threatening calls about warrants for arrest for unpaid taxes. The IRS does not collect taxes in this manner.
  • Learn to spot suspicious links in emails. Check the “From” header in any email received – if the name of the author of the email does not match the author’s email address in the header, this is a sign of a scam. Also, hover your computer cursor over a link in your email without clicking the link itself. By doing this, the address for the link will appear on your screen. If it is different from the address the email purports to come from (a bank, or government organization), this is a sign of a scam.

Scammers are using the health crisis to steal money in other ways, even posing as volunteers requesting donations for disaster relief organizations. If you wish to make a donation to a charity, contact the charity directly and inquire about the best way to help. The Governor’s Office provides an excellent resource for Mainers looking to donate or volunteer: www.maine.gov/governor/mills/covid-19/maine-helps

The Bureau of Financial Institutions has a consumer library with helpful information about how consumers can spot and avoid financial scams. Also, the Bureau’s Consumer Outreach Specialist is available to answer any consumer questions related to financial scams or accounts in general. The Bureau’s phone number is 207-624-8570. The website is www.maine.gov/pfr/financialinstitutions.

WHEREAS, the 130th Maine Legislature unanimously passed L.D. 1861, An Act to Establish the Safe Homes Program, and as Governor, I signed the bill into law on April 7, 2022; and

WHEREAS, this bipartisan law promotes the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms and other dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and

WHEREAS, the Safe Homes Program is an optional, voluntary grant program that builds on the work of L.D. 1140, An Act To Establish a Sales Tax Exemption for the Purchase of Firearm Safety Devices, by making storage devices, such as gun safes, more affordable for people who want to buy them; and

WHEREAS, the Safe Homes Program Fund will provide grants for purchasing safety devices for the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms, and dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and 

WHEREAS, according to a report by the U.S. CDC, there were 181 deaths by firearms in the State of Maine in 2024, with over 86 percent of the deaths the result of suicide; and 

WHEREAS, in 2025, there were 390 confirmed and suspected fatal drug overdoses, 20.4 percent lower than the total confirmed fatal overdoses for 2024; and

WHEREAS, by ensuring that firearms and prescription drugs are properly stored and secured, this law will reduce accidental gun deaths, prevent suicide, and improve public health; and

WHEREAS, in accordance with 1 MRSA § 150-R, the month of September of each year is designated as Safe Homes Awareness Month to raise awareness of the importance of safety in the home and the assistance that is available through the Safe Homes Program established in Title 25, section 7001;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 2026 as

Safe Homes Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance, promote the proper storage of prescription drugs and firearms, and learn more about the assistance available through the Safe Homes Program.

MaineCare Comprehensive Benchmarking Report Initiation Notice

Aug 31, 2026

The Department initiated a comprehensive rate benchmarking report, as required by MRS Title 22 §3173-J. Rate reform law requires that, every four years, the Department compare MaineCare rates to the rates paid by the following:

  • Medicare
  • At least five comparison Medicaid states
  • Any appropriate Maine commercial payers

Interested parties will have the opportunity for public review and comment. The final report will be available on the MaineCare Rate System Reform webpage.

For questions please contact Megan Scott, MaineCare’s Legislative and Reform Coordinator.

Looking Ahead: Eligibility-Dedicated Data Feed to Support MaineCare Renewals and Enrollment

Sep 04, 2026

Two weeks ago, we announced communications support for MaineCare partners and providers regarding changes the federal government is making to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program) eligibility. This message provides an early look at planned data-sharing that will help the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) verify information needed for MaineCare eligibility. Our goal is to help eligible Mainers keep their coverage and access to services with as little disruption as possible.

No action is needed now. We are sharing this information early to make providers aware of what is being planned. We will share more information as plans and timelines are finalized.

DHHS will continue to use administrative data sources it has access to as much as possible to support automatic (“passive”) renewals for MaineCare members. Federal changes to eligibility mean we need additional information to help more eligible members maintain their MaineCare coverage. This data will help Mainers continue to benefit from MaineCare, which in turn will help providers minimize the impact of these federal Medicaid cuts on their revenue and on their charity and uncompensated care.

Clinical Data Will Help People Stay Enrolled in MaineCare

Electronic health record (EHR) systems contain clinical data that Maine and numerous other states are planning to use to help exempt Medicaid applicants and members with work-limiting health conditions from Work Requirements. In Maine, this data will support MaineCare eligibility determination activities administered by the Office for Family Independence (OFI). DHHS intends to partner with providers to collect this information through HealthInfoNet, the State’s contractor for this work. HealthInfoNet will identify indicators of exemptions from work requirements by collecting and processing this clinical data from providers. Using clinical data alongside claims and other administrative data to generate more timely and comprehensive information will help keep Mainers enrolled in MaineCare. We will refer to the data sent to HealthInfoNet for this purpose as the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed.

Until the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed is established we will be basing automatic exceptions for work-limiting health conditions on claims data alone in order to meet implementation deadlines.

This Data Sharing Will Be Separate from the Health Information Exchange

The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be separate from the health information exchange (HIE) data that many providers already share with HealthInfoNet.

The eligibility-dedicated data feed will include only the information needed to support MaineCare eligibility activities. This information will be stored separately from HIE data. It will not be available through HealthInfoNet’s clinical portal or through analytics tools used by some provider organizations. The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be used only in support of OMS and OFI activities associated with eligibility.

Key details to note:

  • The steps needed for a provider to establish this new data feed will vary by provider organization. For example, some provider organizations already have a data feed with HealthInfoNet that can be used as a starting point. Capabilities of the organization’s EHR vendor or technology support may also affect the work needed to establish the data feed. Providers eligible for relevant Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding may consider using this funding for these costs, as determined by the allowable uses of specific RHTP opportunities.
  • We expect it will take the majority of provider organizations two to four months to build their eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed with HealthInfoNet. This time range will be dependent on provider organization’s or vendor’s availability to engage with HealthInfoNet. We expect it will take less time than building a typical HIE data sharing connection with HealthInfoNet.
  • Clinical care teams are not expected to need to take additional steps to send this information as part of their day-to-day work. Once the data feed is established, the identified data categories will be shared automatically with HealthInfoNet.
  • Broad categories of exemptions in statute for work-limiting health conditions include those who are blind or disabled, have a substance use disorder, disabling mental disorder, or complex medical condition. DHHS continues to work with the federal government to clarify data related to these categories that may assist states to automatically exempt individuals, including information related to a person’s ability to work. Kinds of data may include demographic information, diagnosis indicators, encounter or event indicators, and billing codes, among others.

More Information Will Be Coming – No Action Needed Now The Department and HealthInfoNet will distribute instructions for provider organizations to opt into this initiative and implement the eligibility-dedicated data feed. Future communications will include information such as:

  • Which provider types will be prioritized for establishing these connections
  • How providers can participate
  • The types of information that will be needed
  • Technical requirements and specifications
  • Onboarding and implementation steps
  • Timelines

item.title: Management Track Assessment for American Plaice and Gulf of Maine Haddock; Public Meeting
item.description: NMFS will convene the Management Track Assessment Peer Review Meeting for the purpose of reviewing American plaice and Gulf of Maine haddock stocks. The Management Track Assessment Peer Review is a formal scientific peer-review process for evaluating and presenting stock assessment results to managers for fish stocks in the offshore U.S. waters of the northwest Atlantic. Assessments are prepared by the lead stock assessment scientist and reviewed by an independent panel of stock assessment experts. The public is invited to attend the presentations and discussions between the review panel and the scientists who have participated in the stock assessment process.

Temporary Changes to Referral and Authorization Processes Ending November 30, 2026

Sep 08, 2026

Beginning December 1, 2026, the Department will require members to complete a Single Assessment within the past 12 months before processing referrals, prior authorization requests, and continued stay reviews for children’s medium- and high-intensity services. 

As previously communicated, the Department temporarily reinstated direct-to-provider referral and prior authorization processes while operational challenges with the Single Assessment process were being addressed. That temporary process will end November 30, 2026. 

The Single Assessment process has stabilized significantly, with assessments now completed in an average of 7.5 business days after a request is submitted. 

Thank you for your continued partnership with the Single Assessment process.

item.title: Maine Logger’s Day - October 12
item.description: WHEREAS , the logging industry has served as an economic driver and cultural tradition in Maine for centuries; and WHEREAS , the logging industry creates rural jobs and provides revenue for local communities, contributing $534 million to the state’s economy annually; and WHEREAS , loggers provide renewable material for products used by people in Maine every day; and WHEREAS , loggers are the root of Maine’s $8.3 billion forest economy; and WHEREAS , loggers are the means by which healthy and responsible forest management plans are accomplished; and WHEREAS , logging helps keep Maine’s forests healthy, which support vital animal habitats, protect watersheds, sequester carbon, provide recreational opportunities, and limit wildfires; and WHEREAS , logging provides for healthy forests through regeneration to ensure the sustainability of the industry for future generations of Maine people; NOW THEREFORE , be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 12, 2026 as Maine Logger’s Day throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance. In testimony whereof, I have caused the Great Seal of the State to be hereunto affixed GIVEN under my hand at Augusta this tenth day of September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

WHEREAS, the logging industry has served as an economic driver and cultural tradition in Maine for centuries; and

Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Program Publishes Actuarial Report, First Claims Report

October 1, 2026

For Immediate Release: Oct. 1, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

Actuarial report projects PFML Trust Fund will remain stable for the next 10 years

AUGUSTA - The Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) program has published its second annual actuarial report, as well as its first claims report on Oct. 1, 2026.

PFML became law in 2023 and is a statewide program that provides eligible workers with up to 12 weeks of paid leave for medical, parental, family care, military family or safe leave.

The PFML program began accepting claims on March 30, 2026, and began paying benefits on May 1, 2026. This initial claims report covers the program's first three months of claims activity, from March 30 through June 30, 2026. Future claims reports will be published annually and will cover a full year of claims activity.

Highlights of the reports include:

  • The PFML Trust Fund remains solvent and based on updated revenue and claim expenditure, is projected to remain stable for the next 10 years.
  • The program received 8,376 applications between March 30 and June 30, 2026.
  • Among the claims approved, medical leave was the most common reason, followed by welcoming a new child and caring for a family member. Other leave reasons represented a very small portion of the overall claim volume.

"We are excited to see the PFML Program effectively off the ground and helping Maine workers and businesses through life's big moments, both now and for years to come," said PFML Director Luke Monahan.

More information on the PFML program, including how to apply, can be found on the program's website: https://www.maine.gov/paidleave/

Employees, employers and self-employed individuals with questions can call 207-621-5024 between8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. Employees can send a message through the Benefits Application Portal, while employers and self-employed individuals can send a message through the Maine Paid Leave Contributions Portal.

item.title: US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather
item.description: LITTLE ROCK, AR – A U.S. Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. violated the Federal Railroad Safety Act when it removed from service and later terminated a North Little Rock yardman who notified management of nearby lightning and federal safety standards. OSHA determined that the employee voiced concerns about nearby lightning, cited OSHA and NOAA lightening safety guidelines, initiated a safety stand-down, and refused to work until the storm passed. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. Union Pacific terminated his employment on May 30, 2024.On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees. Union Pacific filed objections to OSHA’s order and has requested a hearing before a U.S. Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge.OSHA’s Whistleblower Protection Program enforces 25 whistleblower statutes that protect employees from retaliation for reporting violations of workplace airline, anti-money laundering, commercial motor carrier, consumer product, criminal antitrust, environmental, financial reform, food safety, health insurance reform, maritime, motor vehicle safety, nuclear, pipeline, public transportation agency, railroad, safety and health, securities, and tax laws.Editor’s note: The U.S. Department of Labor does not release the names of employees involved in whistleblower complaints.
